app.name: ProofFlow
app.tagline: Prove your API still does what it did yesterday.

auth.signInSubtitle: Pick up where the last run left off.
auth.signUpSubtitle: The first account also creates a workspace.
auth.invalidCredentials: That email and password do not match an account.
auth.lockedOut: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
auth.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords are not the same.
auth.emailTaken: An account already uses that email.
auth.deniedTitle: You do not have access to that
auth.deniedBody: Your role in this workspace does not include this action. An owner or admin can change it.
auth.point1Body: Run an endpoint, approve the response, and ProofFlow remembers it — field by field, with the parts that change every time marked as changing.
auth.point2Body: Sign in, read a list, pick one from it, create something, check it, delete it again. Drag the steps together and pass each one's output to the next.
auth.point3Body: Not a wall of red text. Which field, what it was, what it is now, and whether that was allowed.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.role_TestDesigner_help: Builds and runs tests, proposes baselines.
workspace.role_Runner_help: Runs existing tests and reads the results.

project.title: Projects
project.subtitle: One project per system you test.
project.nameHint: What is this system called? For example, «Orders API».
project.descriptionHint: One line, so the next person knows what this covers.
project.accentHint: Only used to tell projects apart at a glance.
project.slugHint: Appears in links and in exported files.
project.deleteBody: Every environment, scenario, baseline and run in «{0}» goes with it. This cannot be undone.

empty.title: No projects yet
empty.body: A project holds the environments, scenarios and baselines for one system under test.

project.archiveHint: Archiving hides the project from lists. Nothing is deleted, and it can be brought back at any time.

empty.title: Nothing has run yet
empty.body: Create a project, point it at an endpoint, and the first result will appear here.

audit.title: Activity
audit.subtitle: Every change that matters, and who made it.

empty.title: Nothing recorded yet
empty.body: Changes to projects, environments, baselines and members appear here.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: The action did not complete. Nothing was changed.
error.404body: The link may be old, or the thing it pointed at may have been deleted.
error.403title: You do not have access to that
error.403body: Your role in this workspace does not include this action.
error.500body: The problem was recorded. Trying again is safe — nothing was half-saved.
error.invalidEmail: That does not look like an email address.

projectHome.title: This project is ready for its first environment
projectHome.body: Point it at a base URL, then run an endpoint and save what came back. Environments, scenarios and baselines all hang off this page.

environment.subtitle: One entry per place the system under test runs.
environment.newHint: Give it a name and where it lives. Everything else has a safe default.
environment.kindHint: Presentation and defaults only — the runner treats them alike.
environment.baseUrlHint: What the base-URL reference resolves to. The trailing slash is removed for you.
environment.baseUrlInvalid: That is not a complete address. It needs a scheme, like https://.
environment.maxRedirectsHint: Beyond this, a redirect is treated as a loop.
environment.allowedHostsHint: One per line. A leading *. covers subdomains but not the bare domain. Empty means only the base URL's own host.
environment.reach: What this environment is allowed to do
environment.privateNetwork.hint: Lets requests reach loopback and internal addresses. Cloud metadata endpoints stay blocked either way.
environment.invalidCertificate.hint: For a staging box with a self-signed certificate. Nothing will warn you again once this is on.
environment.isProduction.hint: A failure here is an incident. Runs ask for confirmation, and destructive cleanup refuses without an explicit opt-in.
environment.deleted: «{0}» is gone, with its variables and secrets.
environment.deleteBody: «{0}» goes, and so do the variables and secrets scoped to it. This cannot be undone.

empty.title: No environments yet
empty.body: An environment is a base URL plus the variables, secrets and limits that go with it. Most projects have one per place they deploy.

environment.productionWarning: This is a production environment. Comparing sends a real request to it.
environment.title: Environment

variable.subtitle: Values a request can refer to. Nothing here is hidden — use a secret for anything that should be.
variable.inherited.hint: Set once for the project. Editing it changes every environment.
variable.nameShape: Start with a letter or underscore, then letters, digits or underscores.
variable.deleteBody: Anything referring to «{0}» will stop resolving.

empty.body: No variables yet. Add one and refer to it from any request.

secret.subtitle: Encrypted, never shown in a list, never in an export, and masked wherever a run writes it down.
secret.unreadable: That secret could not be decrypted
secret.deleteBody: Anything referring to «{0}» will stop resolving, and the value cannot be recovered.

empty.body: No secrets yet. Add one and refer to it by name — the value is encrypted and never rendered back.

request.title: Request
request.subtitle: Build one request, send it, and look at what came back. Nothing here is saved to the project.
request.productionConfirm: «{0}» is production. Send this request against it?
request.unresolved: Some references could not be resolved, so nothing was sent.
request.unresolvedHint: A red reference does not exist in the selected environment.

noEnvironments.title: No environment to send against
noEnvironments.body: A request needs somewhere to go. Add an environment with a base URL, then come back — you can also send to a full address without one.

response.empty: Nothing sent yet. Fill in an address and press Send.
response.tooLarge: This response is too large to show as a tree without freezing the page. The raw view has all of it.

failure.Timeout: Raise the timeout in this environment's settings, or check whether the endpoint is genuinely slow.
failure.DnsFailure: Check the base URL for a typo, and that the host resolves from this machine.
failure.Refused: The server is reachable but nothing is listening on that port.
failure.Certificate: If this environment uses a self-signed certificate, allow it in the environment settings.
failure.TooManyRedirects: Raise the redirect limit in this environment's settings, or fix the loop.
failure.ResponseTooLarge: Raise the response size limit in this environment's settings.
failure.BlockedByPolicy: Add the host to this environment's allowed list, or turn on private-network reach — cloud metadata addresses stay blocked either way.
failure.Unresolved: Every reference has to exist before a request can be built.
failure.Unknown: Trying again is safe — nothing was half-sent.

baseline.subtitle: What correct looked like, and what has moved since.

empty.title: No baseline recorded yet
empty.body: A baseline is a response you have read and agreed is right. Send a request, look at what comes back, and save it.

baseline.requestHelp: Stored with the baseline so it can be sent again and compared. References are kept unresolved, so a rotated token does not break it.
baseline.noRequest: This baseline has no request stored, so it cannot be replayed.
baseline.awaitingReview: Version {0} is waiting to be approved. Until it is, comparisons still run against the approved version.
baseline.approvalNeededBySomeoneElse: Your role cannot approve a baseline.
baseline.approved: Version {0} is now the approved baseline.
baseline.nameTaken: A baseline called {0} already exists in this project.
baseline.compareExpired: That comparison is no longer being held. Compare again, then accept.
baseline.compareEmpty: Nothing compared yet. Press Compare to send the request and see what moved.
baseline.needsApproved: This baseline has no approved version yet, so there is nothing to compare against.
baseline.versionProposed: Version {0} proposed. It needs approval before it becomes the baseline.
baseline.saveAsHelp: Stores this response as what correct looks like. The request is stored with it, so the same call can be checked again later.
baseline.descriptionPlaceholder: What this response is meant to prove

diff.title: Differences
diff.invalidRules: These rules could not be read and were skipped: {0}

rule.none: No rules yet, so every field has to match exactly.
rule.help: A rule says which differences do not count. Anything without a rule has to match exactly.
rule.compareAgain: The rules changed, so the comparison on screen is out of date. Compare again.
rule.suggestionsTitle: {0} fields look like they change on their own
rule.suggestionsHelp: Nothing here is applied until you tick it and save. Each one stops a field from being checked, so read before you agree.

matcher.Exact.help: The value has to be identical to the approved one. This is what applies when no rule is written.
matcher.Ignore.help: The value is not looked at. What a timestamp or a generated id gets.
matcher.Exists.help: The field has to be there. What it holds is not checked.
matcher.NotExists.help: The field must not appear. For one that was removed on purpose.
matcher.TypeOnly.help: A string stays a string, a number stays a number. The value itself may change.
matcher.IsNull.help: The field has to be there and hold null.
matcher.IsNotNull.help: The field has to hold something — anything but null.
matcher.Regex.help: The value has to match the regular expression. For an id with a known shape.
matcher.Contains.help: The value has to contain this text somewhere.
matcher.StartsWith.help: The value has to begin with this text.
matcher.EndsWith.help: The value has to end with this text.
matcher.NumericTolerance.help: The number may differ from the approved one by up to this much. For a score that rounds differently elsewhere.
matcher.NumericRange.help: The number has to fall between these two, whatever was approved.
matcher.DateTolerance.help: The instant may differ from the approved one by up to this many seconds.
matcher.JsonSubset.help: Every approved field has to be present with the same value. Extra fields are allowed.
matcher.ArrayOrdered.help: The default for a list: first against first, second against second.
matcher.ArrayUnordered.help: The list may come back shuffled. For anything a database returns unsorted.
matcher.ArrayMatchByKey.help: Items are lined up by the field you name and then compared, so a reordered list reports what moved instead of calling every row different.
matcher.ArrayCount.help: Only the number of items is checked, against a minimum and a maximum.
matcher.CaseInsensitive.help: Compared as text, with upper and lower case treated as the same.
matcher.Trimmed.help: Whitespace at the start and end is removed before comparing.

dynamic.Timestamp: Looks like a date or a time
dynamic.TraceId: Looks like a trace or request id
dynamic.ExpiringUrl: Looks like a link that expires
dynamic.DiffersBetweenRuns: Came back different on two runs of the same request

dataset.subtitle: The inputs a test runs against, one row at a time.
dataset.nameTaken: A data set called {0} already exists in this project.

empty.title: No data set yet
empty.body: A data set is a list of inputs — two thousand identifiers, or five. Paste them in and each one becomes a call.

dataset.noKeyColumn: Without a key column, rows are identified by their position — which changes the first time the list is sorted, and re-points every approved answer at a different input.
dataset.duplicateKeys: {0} keys appear more than once ({1}…). Each input can only have one approved answer, so duplicates will be numbered apart.
dataset.blankKeys: {0} rows have no value in the key column and will fall back to their position.
dataset.versionsHelp: A version is frozen once anything has run against it. Saving edits creates the next one.
dataset.showingFirst: Showing the first {0} of {1} rows. The rest are saved and will run; a set this size is imported rather than typed.
dataset.pasteHelp: Out of a spreadsheet, a database client, or a list somebody sent you. ProofFlow works out the shape and shows you what it read before anything is imported.
dataset.noRows: Nothing here yet. Paste your inputs above, or add a row.

capture.title: Sweep
capture.subtitle: Every input, sent once, and what came back.

empty.title: No sweep yet
empty.body: A sweep sends the baseline's request once for every row of a data set, and files what comes back for review.

capture.keyboardHelp: Press j and k to move between samples, a to approve, r to reject, x to select.
capture.noResponse: This sample has no response, so there is nothing to compare.

wizard.title: Guided setup
wizard.subtitle: From an endpoint to a regression test, one question at a time.
wizard.urlHint: References in double braces are filled in per run: the environment's address, and the current row of the data set.
wizard.sendBody: Send it once and read what comes back. Come back here when the response looks right.
wizard.noBaseline: No baseline yet. Send the request, then save the response as one.
wizard.createDataSet: Create a data set from these {0} rows
wizard.sweepBody: This sends the request once for every one of the {0} rows. Nothing is approved by it — capturing records what the API does, and whether that is right is the next question.
wizard.rulesBody: If the same field differs in every sample, it is a field that changes on its own. A rule says so once, instead of you saying it two thousand times.
wizard.doneBody: Run the sweep again whenever you want to know whether anything moved. What you approved is what it compares against.
wizard.title.baseline: What does a correct answer look like?
wizard.title.data: Which inputs should it run over?
wizard.help.endpoint: The address and the method. Use double braces where a value changes per environment or per row.
wizard.help.environment: An environment carries the base address, the variables and the limits the request runs under.
wizard.help.send: Sending once, by hand, is how you find out the address is wrong before two thousand calls do.
wizard.help.baseline: A baseline is a response you have read and agreed is right. Everything later is compared against it.
wizard.help.data: One row per call. Pick a set you already have, or paste a new list.
wizard.help.sweep: This makes real calls to a real API. Nothing is approved by it.
wizard.help.review: Approve the ones that are right and reject the ones that are not. What you approve becomes the answer for that input.
wizard.help.rules: Some fields change on their own — a timestamp, a generated id. A rule stops them counting as differences.
wizard.help.done: The test exists. Run the sweep again whenever you want to know whether anything moved.
wizard.defineHelp: For a test that runs over many inputs there is no single response to save — each input has its own. This records the request; the answers come from the sweep.
wizard.noSweepYet: Go back a step and run the sweep first.
